Selecting photographs for your brand

Build a useful image collection by balancing story, variety and consistency across different channels.

Charlot Crea31 October 20261 min readSample article
In this articleChoose for the storyBalance context and detailCheck the intended formatsKeep an organised library

Choose for the story

The most striking single photograph is not always the best opening image for a collection. Start with the message the selection needs to communicate. Identify the main subject, the supporting details and the moments that make the brand recognisable. Give each image a role.

Balance context and detail

Wide views introduce a place or situation. Closer frames can communicate texture, expression and atmosphere. Review how the selection moves between them. Repeated angles may reduce the usefulness of a collection even when each photograph works well on its own.

Check the intended formats

A photograph should be assessed in the layout where it will appear. Consider the space needed for text, the differences between desktop and mobile and whether a vertical version is available. Preserve the composition rather than applying the same automatic crop to every image.

Keep an organised library

Use clear filenames and record the approved uses, versions and credit information for the collection. Keep original deliveries separate from resized exports. A well organised library makes future updates easier and helps a team use images consistently across a website, presentation or campaign.
